clue.text: Well, Communist should be allowed to live

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
Red is the stock term for a Communist

explanation.surface: A political question: should a Communist at the health spa be permitted to go on living?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spared escapes death, so they have been permitted to survive.

clue.text: Insignificant stuff — I bottle it in test

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces before it inside the word for a test

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a vial is a small glass bottle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a lab exercise of bottling a sample as trivial nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia and trifles are matters of little importance, insignificant stuff.

clue.text: Desire to include grandma in agreement

indicators.note: to include means the word for desire takes another piece within it

parts.note: to covet is to desire
nan is an informal British word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone longs to bring their grandmother into a family deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding pact or contract.

clue.text: Condescend to remove an old feature of organ

indicators.note: to remove signals that a letter is taken away from the word for condescend

parts.note: to stoop is to condescend, lower oneself

explanation.surface: An organist deigns to rip out an antiquated part of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ stops are the knobs or levers that bring sets of pipes into play.

clue.text: Gave nothing to men at sea? Hurry up!

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A captain gave his sailors no shore leave, then barked at them to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic command to be quick, to start moving faster.

clue.text: Creator? Not now

definitions.meaning: one who forms or shapes something is a creator
something no longer so, belonging to the past

explanation.surface: A curt exchange: someone asks about the maker and is told it's not the time.
explanation.definitionFit: One who forms is a maker; as an adjective it means previous, of an earlier time.

clue.text: Persistence beginning to rankle in annoying character

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for an annoying person

parts.note: git is a British insult for an irritating, contemptible person

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Dogged persistence in an irritating person starts to grate.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the staying power to keep going.

clue.text: Line in what actress responds to indicates heroic figure

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the phrase built from the actress's prompts

parts.note: an actress reacts to her cues, the prompts that signal her turn to speak

explanation.surface: A theatre note: one line in the actress's prompts reveals the play's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as HER plus CUES, the lines an actress waits for.
explanation.definitionFit: The strongman of Greek and Roman myth is the archetypal hero.

clue.text: Cut some lessons, holding out for usual score

indicators.note: holding means the word for cut keeps another word within it

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
forth means out, as in go forth
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A truant skips classes, holding out for a typical grade.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, par is the standard score for a course, hence the idiom for what is normal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means what is normal or expected, literally the standard golf score.

clue.text: Cancel, getting OK to be replaced by university show

indicators.note: to be replaced by signals that a stretch of letters is swapped for another

parts.note: to revoke is to cancel or withdraw
the letters O and K, taken as written

explanation.surface: A university show was cancelled, then given approval to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs.

clue.text: Realistic photo capturing two bits of fabric

indicators.note: capturing means the word for a photo holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: pic is a short informal word for a photograph
a rag and a mat are two pieces of cloth

explanation.surface: A lifelike photograph captures a couple of scraps of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pragmatic means practical and down-to-earth, dealing with things as they are.

clue.text: Agitated Britten finally added a solo aria with no life at all

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the gathered letters are shaken into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: An excited Benjamin Britten tacked a solo aria onto a lifeless piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from Britten; the rest of the fodder is ADDED A SOLO ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something utterly, unmistakably lifeless.

clue.text: Financial officer has some hesitation about one location of speech

parts.note: an auditor is an official who checks financial accounts
I is the Roman numeral for one
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An accountant hems and haws over a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall where an audience sits to hear speakers is a place for talks and speeches.

clue.text: Weather device: article chaps set up before remote storms

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word for chaps is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: storms means rages wildly, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A forecaster's piece about chaps setting up before distant storms.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures wind speed, used by meteorologists.

clue.text: Tense women with exotic diets getting misrepresented

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: exotic means strange and outlandish, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uptight women on strange diets find their views misreported.
explanation.definitionFit: A distorted account is one whose facts have been bent out of shape.

clue.text: Redrafted one post about a source of stir

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the single letter
redrafted means rewritten, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An editor rewrites a single post on a source of controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redrafted' gives TESPOON, and 'about' wraps that round A; 'stir' is the verb, not a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is what one stirs tea or coffee with.

clue.text: Newspaper produced by retired journalists?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer working
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A paper written by former reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is a British national daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is one of Britain's national tabloid papers.

clue.text: Item to be kept secret? Mostly dull fool slipping up

indicators.note: slipping up in a down clue means the assembled letters are read upwards, backwards
mostly means the last letter of the word for dull is dropped

parts.note: drowsy means sluggish and dull
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A dim-witted fool blunders and lets a secret slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A login code must be kept private, so it is a thing to keep secret.

clue.text: No party, it seems, will offer emergency response

definitions.text: No party, it seems, will offer emergency response

parts.words: No party, it seems, will offer emergency response
parts.note: the proverb says that in trouble one takes any refuge going; whimsically, a port is a party drink and in a storm no party is fussy

explanation.surface: No political party seems to have a crisis plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb means any help is welcome in an emergency; 'party' tempts towards politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means that in a crisis one accepts whatever help or refuge is available.

clue.text: Hard to understand ordinary old man quite without attraction

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: without means the word for attraction is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: it means sex appeal, attraction

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark: an ordinary old fellow quite lacking charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque writing or reasoning is obscure, not clear to the reader.

clue.text: Elevated benefit in my song?

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the word my
elevated in a down clue means the word for benefit is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the dole is state unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.surface: A songwriter wonders if a lofty welfare theme belongs in their song.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody is a tune, an air or song.

clue.text: Source of ink to mark sheep — arcane symbol?

parts.note: a pen delivers ink
to tag is to label or mark
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer uses a pen to brand a sheep with a mysterious sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-pointed star is a sign used in magic and the occult.

clue.text: Some stoner dude?

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a guy is just a pothead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is a man of some kind; this kind is the socially awkward geek, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Kind to support military's first exploit

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means the piece below holds up the one above, so it comes after
first picks the opening letter of the word military's

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: Someone offers to back the army's first operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk something is to take as much advantage of it as possible.

clue.text: Little left after eating husband's cheese

indicators.note: eating means the outer pieces take another letter inside them

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Not much is left after a husband has tucked into the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is made in a large round form, which is sold by the round.

clue.text: Literary figure we both know?

parts.note: a friend known to both of us is a shared acquaintance, and the phrase is a Dickens title

explanation.surface: Two people discuss a writer they both have met.
explanation.walkthrough: The literary figure is a work of literature, Dickens's last completed novel, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's last finished novel bears this title, which also describes a shared acquaintance.
